PRESENT:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, MAZA

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia,
Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Parks and
Recreation Macias, Director of Library LohGuan, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Chief of Police Kennedy

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

2.  HISTORIC PRESERVATION PROGRAM UPDATE – F2M20-51

  Director of Community Development HO introduced the item. Alexandra PERLMAN & Mary
  RINGHOFF with the Historic Resources Group, made a presentation, a copy of which is on
  file in the City Clerks Office. The City of Alhambra is currently working with Historic Resources
  Group (HRG) and Architectural Resources Group (ARG) on a citywide historic resources
  survey. Informed by the City’s historic context statement completed in 2022, the historic
  resources survey identifies, records, and evaluates historic properties that were built prior to
  1980. The survey will assist in the preservation and rehabilitation of historic resources and
  serve as a planning tool. HRG’s Alexandra Perlman and ARG’s Mary Ringhoff will be
  presenting an update on the progress of the citywide historic resources survey and explain
  the next steps as we transition into Phase 3, which will involve drafting a new ordinance. The
  presentation will provide a brief overview of the Historic Preservation Program, provide details
  on how the citywide historic resources survey was conducted, briefly explain the initial draft
  findings, and explain how the survey will inform the creation of the ordinance in the next phase.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor PÉREZ inquired about the number of community meetings
  scheduled and what will be discussed. Ms. Perlman responded to questions.

  Councilmember MALONEY referenced the previously adopted historic context statement and
  suggested utilizing it for the upcoming community meetings. Ms. Perlman responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember LEE inquired how they determined which properties are eligible for the
  program, how the inventory of properties is finalized, and what will be discussed at the
  community meetings. Ms. Perlman and Director of Community Development Ho responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STALDER inquired about the research done on older properties
  in the City. Ms. Perlman responded to questions.

  Mayor MAZA discussed the make-up of the properties that were identified for the program,
  inquired if other single-family homes will be identified in the future, and discussed the number
  of properties identified as opposed to other cities. Ms. Perlman responded to questions.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this informational report.

3.  LEGISLATIVE UPDATE ON SB 567 (DURAZO): TENANT PROTECTIONS – F2M23-7

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report. On May 22, 2023, the City Council
  adopted an Urgency Ordinance (O2M23-4811) establishing a temporary moratorium on
  certain “no fault” residential evictions due to a property owners’ intent to substantially remodel
  a tenant’s unit in the City of Alhambra. Pursuant to the Ordinance, the City Council intended
  to provide additional time (through December 31, 2023) to study appropriate tenant protections
  for Alhambra, particularly since the California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
  contains eviction exceptions for demolishing or substantially remodeling a rental unit. After a
  tenancy is terminated for rehabilitation, an owner could raise rent on the newly-remodeled unit
  in excess of AB 1482’s rent cap. In February 2023, citing similar loopholes in AB 1482, Senator
  Maria Elena Durazo introduced SB 567, which adds requirements and restrictions for evictions
  related to substantial remodels. The bill, as amended, also includes other enhancements
  including further defining property owner, noticing requirements, and violation damages. Staff
  2
9-11-23
   will provide the Council with an update on the provisions of SB 567 as it relates to substantial
  remodel evictions as well as the bill’s status in the California legislature.

  Public Comment:

  1) Brian Otis discussed expressed support for SB 567 and encouraged the Council to
  eliminate the temporary moratorium on certain “no fault” residential evictions.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE discussed SB 567 and what was included in the proposed
  legislation.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER expressed hope that the Governor will sign the bill.

  Councilmember MALONEY thanked Senator Durazo for taking on this proposed legislation.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ stated the City should wait until action is taken on the bill before deciding
  what to do with the temporary moratorium.

  Mayor MAZA expressed support for SB 567.

  Action Taken:  City Council received a report regarding state tenant protections under
  SB 567 (Durazo) and provided feedback specific to Alhambra’s recent Temporary Moratorium
  on “no fault” evictions due to substantial remodels and the permanent protections as
  established under the Durazo bill.

  the appointments stay current and to ensure that any adjustments are made, if needed.

  Discussion: Mayor MAZA noted that himself and Councilmember ANDRADE-
  STADLER have switched roles on the San Gabriel Valley Association of Governments and
that he will be the delegate moving forward and Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER will be
the alternate.

  Action Taken:  City Council voted to approve the City Council appointments to various
  external boards/commissions; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M23-156)

6.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON MARENGO AVENUE – F2M23-66,
  RFP2M23-23

  The 10-inch cast iron water main on Marengo Avenue between Grand Avenue and Alhambra
  Road was installed in 1966. This segment of water main has history of breaks, causing
  interruption of water service and damage to the road. Replacing the water main would greatly
  improve flow, firefighting capabilities, and overall system reliability.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  Professional Engineering Design Services for the Water Main Replacement Project on
  Marengo Avenue, with proposals due no later than 4:00 p.m. on Thursday, October 5, 2023.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

7.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: SOUTH FIRST STREET PARKING STRUCTURE ELEVATOR
  MODERNIZATION – F2M22-50, C2M22-37, M2M23-157

  On June 27, 2022, the City Council awarded a contract to TK Elevator Company for the South
  First Street Parking Structure Elevator Modernization Project in the amount of $104,538.30.
  The project consisted of replacing mechanical and electrical components such as new power
  unit, elevator controller, new cab interior fan and lighting. Additionally, the project included the
  installation of new vandal resistant call buttons and elevator inner door. A new phase II fire
  alarm recall was installed to meet current safety standards. This project has been inspected
  by staff and all work has been completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and
  specifications. As such, it would be appropriate for the City Council to accept this project as
  complete and instruct that the Notice of Completion be filed with the County of Los Angeles
  Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None

10.  AWARD CONTRACT: SIX COPIERS/PRINT PRINTERS AND ONE FAX FINISHER –
  F2M23-6B, C2M23-75, M2M23-160

  The City, in September 2018, entered into a 5-year lease for Image IV Systems, Inc. copiers
  located in the Alhambra Library. The current lease expires on September 20, 2023. The Library
  Department has the opportunity to piggyback on a cooperative purchase agreement with the
  Association of Education Purchasing Agencies (AEPA) contract IFB#017-B for all-inclusive
  copy/print services excluding paper and staples, and the lease and maintenance of six Konica
  Minolta Bizhub 300i  units. The contract is for a term of 60 months. Per the Alhambra
  Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3), bidding exemption is authorized, and the City may “piggyback”
  onto an existing contract of a government entity. Staff has reviewed the specifications for
  equipment manufactured and distributed by Image IV Systems and finds Konica Minolta
  Bizhub 300i units most appropriate for the City’s needs. The new five-year monthly lease is
  $509.00 per month (excluding applicable sales taxes) totaling 30,590.00 for six new multi-
  function copiers/printers with excess per copy for color and black/white. The lease price
  includes expendable supplies (excluding paper and staples) and maintenance.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the Library Director to enter into a five-year
  lease agreement with Image IV Systems, Inc. for six copiers/printers and one fax finisher to
  replace six existing copiers/printers and one fax finisher for a total of $30,590.00 (excluding
  applicable sales taxes); and, directed staff to take the steps necessary to finalize the Council's
  action. (M2M23-160)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, PÉREZ, MAZA

11.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE ASSOCIATES – F2M22-65,
C2M23-64, M2M23-161

  On July 24, 2023, Environmental Science Associates was awarded a contract to provide the
  Professional California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) for the Alhambra Community
  Center. This amendment is necessary to implement an Environmental Impact Report (“EIR”)
  to CEQA requirements. The original agreement was for a mitigated negative declaration path
  to a final CEQA determination. The EIR process will take approximately 1,000 additional
  professional hours, extend the entitlement schedule, and cost $215,219 in fees. ESA’s
  additional work product includes: preparing a Notice of Preparation and public scoping;
  preparing for and attend a public scoping meeting; preparing the EIR which analyzes the
  project’s potential environmental impacts; creating a comprehensive set of project objectives
  within the Project Description and to identifying alternatives to the Project; submitting the EIR
  for public review; reviewing and responding to all public comments; preparing the final EIR;
  preparing Findings of Fact and Statement of Overriding Considerations; and, preparing the
  EIR’s Notice of Determination.

  Discussion:  None

  Associates (Contract No. C2M23-64) for an additional $215,219 in an amount not to exceed
  $360,219; and, directed staff to undertake the steps to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-161)

12.  ACCEPT GRANT: OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY – TRAFFIC RECORDS IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECT – F2M23-18, M2M23-162

  The goal of the Office of Traffic Safety and Selective Traffic Records Improvement Project
  (TRIP) is to assist the Alhambra Police Department in increasing its contribution to the Office
  of Traffic Safety’s goal of improving overall roadway safety by providing accurate and timely
  data that roadway engineering improvements and traffic safety enforcement operations rely
  on. The Alhambra Police Department intends to utilize funding for the TRIP to upgrade an
  existing electronic collision reporting program to the latest version available that includes the
  capability of exporting complete collision report records to the California Highway Patrol’s
  Statewide Integrated Traffic Records System. The TRIP will allow the Police Department to go
  paperless and save staff time needed to print and send physical copies of the required reports,
  as mandated by the State of California. It will reduce the time for statistical data to be available,
  which will allow for more timely identification of problem areas, improving overall roadway
  safety.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) grant in the
  amount of $24,800; appropriate revenue and expenditure funds in the amount of $24,800;
  authorize the Chief of Police to enter into a contract with the Office of Traffic Safety for grant
  implementation; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M23-162)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, PÉREZ, MAZA

  Absent:  NONE

13.  ACCEPT GRANT: OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY – PEDESTRIAN AND BICYCLE SAFETY
  PROGRAM – F2M23-18, M2M23-163

  The goal of the Office of Traffic Safety and Pedestrian Bicycle Safety Program is to reduce the
  number of individuals killed or injured from collisions involving pedestrians and bicyclists. The
  Alhambra Police Department intends to utilize Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program funding
  for various educational safety programs, including classroom lectures, bicycle rodeos,
  community events, presentations; training for local law enforcement; and for participation in
  programs such as National Walk to School Day, National Bicycle Safety Month, National
  Pedestrian Safety Month and California’s Pedestrian Safety Month.

  Discussion:  None

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS) – F2M23-7

Vice Mayor PÉREZ referenced an earlier public comment and inquired if big rig trucks are allowed to
park on Hellman Ave., expressed appreciation for the historic preservation presentation earlier in the
meeting, discussed the recently adopted gun regulation ordinance by the City of Monterey Park and
requested to bring back an ordinance to an upcoming meeting to pass a moratorium banning the new
sales of fire arms in the City and to ban firearms in public spaces. There was consensus amongst the
Council to bring back a proposed ordinance.

Councilmember MALONEY expressed appreciation for the story of the concentration camp mentioned
by Mr. McCammon.

Councilmember LEE discussed the recent 9/11 ceremony and discussed listing City events in the
Around Alhambra newspaper. City Manager BINNQUIST noted that the City is prohibited from paying
for ads per state law and noted that the Mayor’s Corner article could include outreach for events.

Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER congratulated Edward Elizalde, the new Police Chief of the City
of San Gabriel, discussed the release of the new booster shot for COVID-19, and congratulated Mayor
MAZA on running his first meeting as Mayor.

Mayor MAZA discussed the importance of the zoning code update and requested that the Council
establish a deadline for the Planning Commission to finalize their recommendation to the Council. There
was a consensus amongst the Council to bring back an item to establish a deadline for the zoning
code update.

Mayor MAZA discussed the upcoming Latino Heritage Month Fiesta, discussed the upcoming Compost
Giveaway at Granda Park, highlighted the recently opened “paw-up” dog park at Almansor Park, stated
that the Library is providing free at-home COVID-19 test kits, and discussed the upcoming Autumn
Fest.

ADJOURNMENT: At 7:33 p.m. there being no further business for the Council to transact, the Mayor,
with the consent of the City Council, adjourned their meeting in memory of all those lost on September
11, 2001, to the next regular meeting of the Alhambra City Council is scheduled for Monday,
September 25, 2023 at 6:00 p.m.
